arguments.decision: How should corpus-mode verifiers establish that the corpus is complete?
arguments.evidence: Independent review of the new verifiers (agent finding, reproduced or plausible) reported: (1) corpus mode never asserts the corpus is complete: a mirror with 10 .ptg files removed returned pass with files 538, unpaired .msh/.mih skipped silently; (2) end flags in the middle of a span pass and a lone flag-7 final block is accepted; (3) decode memory grows unbounded for large spans and deinterleave allocates per channel for an empty payload. Measured facts: corpus has 305 spans (largest 80,496 bytes, median 17,520); every span has exactly one end-bit block (206 spans, flag 3) or exactly two (99 spans, flag 1 then flag 7 whose 14 data bytes are all 0x77); milestone formats check already verifies all 990 files by full SHA-256 against an independent archive read; notes/extracted-manifest.tsv holds a 16-hex sha1 prefix per file; milestone issue #2 requires missing required evidence to be incomplete, unsupported items listed, bounded processing, claims limited to what is measured. coverage() reads and hashes all 990 files and takes about 20 seconds; the manifest sha1 prefix check over the relevant files would take a few seconds.
arguments.priorities: Issue #2: missing required evidence is incomplete and the complete corpus is accounted for; keep each check independently runnable; reasonable runtime; smallest correct change.

candidates.description: Assert the expected counts (548 PTG, 56 models, 27 bank pairs, 20 music pairs), fail on unpaired header or payload files, and check each file's sha1 prefix against notes/extracted-manifest.tsv; a count shortfall is incomplete, a hash or pairing mismatch is fail.
Call the milestone corpus_contract.coverage() from each verifier.
Document that completeness is the formats check's job and add nothing.

requirements: A mirror with files removed cannot return pass.
The binding to the archive baseline is checked, not only implied by the five baseline hashes.
